title: Sneak & Snipe: Through the Scope
use: Public website large hero banner only; concept artwork, not gameplay.
prompts: Use case: ads-marketing / stylized-concept. Create a new widescreen hero banner for the indie stealth sniper PC game Sneak & Snipe: Through the Scope. Image 1 is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: retain its sophisticated navy, cream, desaturated teal and small vermilion accents, hand-printed screenprint texture and graphic indie espionage atmosphere. Replace the static composition with a dramatically more dynamic first-person SNIPER SCOPE AIMING view. The player is tracking a fast train from a parallel moving train on a high urban railway bridge. Camera at the sniper's eye, close to a substantial dark metal optic eyepiece dominating the RIGHT 60 percent of the image; a short connected hint of fictional rifle body exits the bottom-right frame. The visible glass has a clear thin mil-dot sniper reticle and one restrained red aiming point, precisely over a small distant armed operative with a red armband visible in a moving train window. It must unmistakably feel like looking THROUGH a mounted riflescope while aiming, not a floating decorative circle, not a camera lens or binoculars. Show no foreground face, body, hands or fingers. Use a bold 10-degree Dutch angle, strong diagonal rails and bridge girders rushing toward a vanishing point, one passing girder slicing the far edge of the optic as an obstruction, and directional print streaks outside the lens. Keep the reticle and target crisp inside the glass, with tangible perspective and modest lens magnification. A compact sunlit city and railway far below add height and parallax; strong near/far layering, tense moment BEFORE firing. No muzzle flash, no bullet impact, no blood or gore. The dark outer optic rim is thick enough to read instantly and stays in the safe image bounds. Composition: the optic center is around 73 percent across and 47 percent down; keep the LEFT 35 percent quiet, dark navy, with low detail and excellent negative space for a website's separately-rendered white title and button. Keep the important target and reticle well within the central-right crop, no critical detail at extreme edges. The diagonal energy should come from the scene, without sacrificing the quiet copy area. Output 16:9 landscape, at least 1920x1080 if possible. Restrained professional indie poster design, screenprint illustration, cinematic composition but NOT photorealistic, NOT glossy AAA AI concept art, NOT comic-book panels. Absolutely NO text, NO lettering, NO logo, NO fake UI labels, NO watermark, NO real weapon brands.

Edit ONLY the scene visible INSIDE the riflescope glass in this image. Keep the entire image outside the glass unchanged, including the physical scope housing, connected rifle, dark copy space on the left, Dutch angle, rushing bridge, city, palette and screenprint texture. Keep the mil-dot reticle and its red central aiming point fixed exactly where they are. Reposition the moving train window and the same distant operative within the optical view so that the red central aiming point sits unmistakably on the operative's UPPER TORSO / chest, with his head just above it. The operative must remain naturally proportioned within the passenger window; red armband readable, a small radio or unbranded tactical equipment, same scale and graphic silhouette, not a close-up portrait. Shift the blurred vertical foreground bridge girder currently blocking the center of the optic to the FAR RIGHT EDGE of the glass, so it frames the moving scene without hiding the operative or reticle center. The result must read instantly as a sniper precisely aiming at a moving target through a mounted scope, with a clear aiming point on the target, before firing. Preserve all existing dynamic perspective, art direction and print grain. No text, no logo, no UI labels, no muzzle flash, no impact, no blood. 16:9 wide hero banner; retain the full uncropped source composition.

Make one precise graphic correction to this finished game-banner illustration: correct the sniper reticle INSIDE THE GLASS ONLY. The current red aiming dot is on the operative's upper chest, which is correct, but the horizontal crosshair incorrectly passes above his head. Move that single thin horizontal mil-dot crosshair DOWN so it intersects the vertical crosshair EXACTLY at the existing red aiming dot on his upper chest. There must be ONE coherent crosshair intersection with the red dot at its intersection, visibly centered on the operative's chest. Remove the old horizontal line above his head entirely, including its old black central intersection. Retain the same fine mil-dot style, slight tilt and line weights. Leave the vertical reticle, the existing red dot and the operative exactly in place. Do not change the scope rim, any train geometry, operative, girder at the right edge, connected rifle, city, print texture, Dutch angle, dark left text area, or anything else. Do not add any other red dots, any words or logos. Preserve the original full image composition and dimensions.
content_type: Concept artwork; not a gameplay screenshot
